searchText: Hi, I've been reading the berlin execution specs in conjunction with the berlin yellow paper and noticed a discrepancy. The execution-specs only invalidate the block if the sender balance can cover the up-front gas_fee: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/cc697f256d281476b9c9f810542e84fb78be2505/src/ethereum/berlin/spec.py#L599-L601 However, in the YP (and client implementations), the tx.value is also added to the gas_fee for this check: https://github.com/ethereum/yellowpaper/blob/7251f10f25fc2a340c51c57e4a71970b525c0691/Paper.tex#L708-L711 A check is done later as part of the EVM https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/cc697f256d281476b9c9f810542e84fb78be2505/src/ethereum/berlin/vm/interpreter.py#L239-L243 which can raise an InsufficientFunds exception. However I believe this results in an exception which sets the gas to 0, which seems like a significant difference compared to the transaction being recognised as invalid earlier. Have I missed something here? Will need to take a closer look at this It'd be a pretty glaring hole if this case wasn't covered by `ethereum-tests`, but certainly possible. The current tests that we run pass either way. Hi, I've been reading the berlin execution specs in conjunction with the berlin yellow paper and noticed a discrepancy. The execution-specs only invalidate the block if the sender balance can cover the up-front gas_fee:
https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/cc697f256d281476b9c9f810542e84fb78be2505/src/ethereum/berlin/spec.py#L599-L601 
However, in the YP (and client implementations), the tx.value is also added to the gas_fee for this check: https://github.com/ethereum/yellowpaper/blob/7251f10f25fc2a340c51c57e4a71970b525c0691/Paper.tex#L708-L711

A check is done later as part of the EVM https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/cc697f256d281476b9c9f810542e84fb78be2505/src/ethereum/berlin/vm/interpreter.py#L239-L243 which can raise an InsufficientFunds exception.
However I believe this results in an exception which sets the gas to 0, which seems like a significant difference compared to the transaction being recognised as invalid earlier.

Have I missed something here?

excerpts.author: gurukamath
excerpts.content: Will need to take a closer look at this

excerpts.author: samwilsn
excerpts.content: It'd be a pretty glaring hole if this case wasn't covered by `ethereum-tests`, but certainly possible.

excerpts.author: gurukamath
excerpts.content: The current tests that we run pass either way. So it appears not to have been covered 🤔
